title: Pool trend sparklines - daily util export (Mar 10-14 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Daily extraction of per-cluster, per-pool GPU utilization with compact sparklines to surface short-term trends. This export is intended for triage meetings and for feeding into the capacity projection job that runs weekly.

Notes summary (top-level):
- Time window: 2026-03-10 00:00 -> 2026-03-14 23:59 (UTC).
- Granularity: 5-minute rollups aggregated to daily median and daily 95th percentile where useful.
- Focus: pool-level headroom and early-warning for clusters trending toward sustained >85% median GPU utilization.
- Special callout: cluster-az3-pool-ml-2 shows steadily increasing weekday spikes; correlated with a new canary training job (ticket INF-5402).

Key metrics included in the sheet columns (CSV-friendly):
- date, cluster_id, pool_name, region, median_gpu_util_pct, p95_gpu_util_pct, running_jobs, queued_jobs, avg_alloc_latency_ms, headroom_pct, preemptible_pct, daily_sparkline (5-point), anomaly_flag, note

Short analytical highlights:
- Global: fleet median utilization across pools increased from 42% -> 51% across the five days; headroom decreased accordingly (median headroom 58% -> 49%).
- US-west pools (pool-ml-1, pool-ml-3): median GPU util rose ~12 percentage points on weekdays; p95 reached 89% on 2026-03-12 for pool-ml-3 (transient but repeated at same time window two days later).
- EMEA: relatively flat usage; a single-day spike in pool-research-1 on 2026-03-11 attributable to a scheduled eval run (linked INF-5419).
- Sustained risk: cluster-az3-pool-ml-2 has median util 78% with p95 at 96% and headroom 4% -> label as yellow (monitor, possible burst request recommended).
- Queue pressure: two pools show growing queued_jobs trend (pool-realtime-1 / pool-batch-2) — these correlate with autoscaling policy caps on dedicated pools.

Actionable recommendations:
1) Short term (next 72h): grant a +10% burst floor to pool-ml-3 in us-west for peak hours (18:00-22:00 UTC) for 3 days while infra triages the canary training.
2) Medium term: schedule capacity add (reserve 8 GPUs) to cluster-az3 (pool-ml-2) to bring median utilization below 65% during weekday load spikes.
3) Policy change: relax autoscale max_instances for pool-realtime-1 from 32 -> 40 to reduce queue spikes; monitor tail latency for 48h post-change.
4) Investigate: the allocation latency outliers in cluster-eu2 on 2026-03-13 — likely API throttling; check IAM/key rotation events and rate-limit metrics.

Observability notes (columns exported to drive, and what remains in OLAP):
- Export includes: per-cluster daily median/p95 stats, running/queued job counts, simple 5-point sparkline (derived from 24h quantiles), allocation latency sample, and preemptible usage fraction.
- Longer timeseries (5m rollups, full 24h curve) remain in ClickHouse / OLAP and are referenced by the ticket links above for deeper drilldowns.

Why this export differs from previous weekly snapshots:
- Compact sparklines attached directly to rows for quick visual triage in the sheet (human-friendly).
- Includes allocation latency and queued_jobs in the same row so scheduling policy impacts are visible without a separate join.
- Explicit anomaly_flag readable by the monitoring lambda to trigger Slack alerts for pool owners.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Aisha: implement temporary burst config for pool-ml-3 (INF-5426).
- Morgan: validate allocation latency traces for cluster-eu2 and confirm/no IAM rate-limit (INF-5430).
- Diego (owner): queue capacity add proposal for cluster-az3 for next PE sync.

notes: This is a working export used in infra standups. Treat as operational: variable formatting, minor gaps allowed. The sheet is regenerated nightly; tickets created for persistent anomalies.
